extracted.intended_audience: poets, dramatists, and aspiring writers of poetry and drama
extracted.subtask_description: Practical norms and craft rules for composing poems and plays: unity of form and content, choice of subject and meter, dramaturgy and staging, diction by character, and audience-aware composition. Focuses on classical models and general principles for producing effective verse and theatre.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity and Homogeneity
rubrics_metrics.description: The work should be consistent and homogeneous from end to end; avoid dream-like, incongruous blends of images or parts that don't fit together.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anti-pattern example: mixing incompatible elements (a maid above, a hideous fish below; 'unions of lamb with tiger, snake with bird'). Ensure every part contributes to a coherent whole.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate Style to Subject (Genre Propriety)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each genre has its own fixed proprieties: comic subjects decline when told in high tragic lines, and the gross Thyestean feast disdains comic vehicle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use high tragic diction for comic material or low comic diction for solemn subjects. Maintain the proper register for the chosen genre; deviations may only be occasional and deliberate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concision and Economy
rubrics_metrics.description: Be concise where needed: the soul takes in short maxims and retains them; pouring more when the vessel is full wastes effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lectures and didactic passages should be brief and pithy. Avoid over-explaining; trim redundance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select and Refine Language
rubrics_metrics.description: Carefully pick words and reject the rest; a dexterous setting can make an old word new; check redundance and harshness and improve by wise refinement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Self-edit: excise words 'devoid of weight' and favor choice terms. Examples: rescue 'choice terms, long hidden' to dignify language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modest Coinage and Neologisms
rubrics_metrics.description: New words may be used if claimed with modesty and if they derive naturally (e.g., from Greek) — usage validates them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Don't invent gratuitous or jarring coinages; follow precedent of Ennius/Cato but be restrained.

rubrics_metrics.name: Match Subject to Authorial Powers
rubrics_metrics.description: Choose a theme equal to your powers; do not attempt a weighty theme that will make your abilities give way.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Better to adapt a known epic to the stage cleverly than to attempt an opus beyond your strength; modesty in theme selection preserves dignity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plot Unity: Beginning, Middle, End
rubrics_metrics.description: Arrange story so beginning, middle, and end agree; avoid windy openings that announce everything (the cyclic opening) and instead enter at the crisis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Don't 'wind your horn' with all background; 'hurry to the crisis' and omit what will not turn to gold under your touch.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character Consistency and Type-Fidelity
rubrics_metrics.description: Characters should be painted in keeping with their established fame or a consistent plan (e.g., Achilles impatient, Medea revengeful).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If inventing a new type, sustain it consistently from start to finish. Avoid lapses that make characters act against their nature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diction Appropriate to Person and Place
rubrics_metrics.description: Speech must fit the speaker: gods should not speak like heroes; youth, elders, nurses, foreign peoples each require distinct styles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tailor vocabulary, syntax, and tone to rank, age, social role, and nationality. Regional or role-appropriate diction increases verisimilitude.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plausible Presentation of Events (Believability)
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep fiction near to truth: treat belief not as caprice; improbable elements must have internal logic (e.g., a vampire must be dead when ripped up).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid fantastical shocks that break belief; the audience must be able to accept what happens within the work's own rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offstage Treatment of Horrors
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not display shocking, disgusting, or unbelievable actions before the public eye (e.g., Medea killing her children).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conceal gruesome deeds and let actors or chorus narrate them; sensational onstage displays generate disgust and shock credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Control of Spectacle and Stage Pageantry
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid overreliance on spectacle, foreign finery, chariots, beasts, and mechanical shows that distract from the poetry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anti-pattern: plays kept down hours for parade of horse and foot, elephants or hybrid beasts that win applause for visuals rather than lines. Let drama and craft, not mere pomp, hold the audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chorus Function and Appropriateness
rubrics_metrics.description: The chorus should sustain the actor, further the plot, be apt and relevant between acts, give counsel, temper wrath, praise justice, conceal secrets, and implore the gods appropriately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choral interludes must be integrated, not mere filler; their music/instrumentation should be simple and moderate in volume.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moderate Use of Musical Accompaniment
rubrics_metrics.description: Flute and chorus accompaniment should be simple, slight, and moderately loud — not trumpet-tongued or overbearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instrumentation should suit audience size and the rustic origins of dramatic song; avoid overpowering brass.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structural Rules for Plays
rubrics_metrics.description: A play should have five acts (no more, no fewer); bring in no god except as a last resource; avoid having four speakers join in discourse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respect classical act structure and avoid deus ex machina unless indispensable. Keep clarity of delivery — don't pack simultaneous speakers into a scene.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enter the Action — Avoid Overlong Exposition
rubrics_metrics.description: Begin at a point that propels the story; don't open like the cyclic with unnecessary preface or distant background.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Launch close to the crisis; let the narrative omit what won't bear transformation under your hand.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adherence to Meter and Rhythmic Suitability
rubrics_metrics.description: Use metres appropriate to the subject (Homeric for heroic, elegiac for complaint/love, iambic for certain discourse), and handle trimeter with care (avoid overloading with spondees).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Study Greek models; false rhythm is easy to hide but harms quality. Keep the natural place of short and long syllables in trimeter; learn from Attius/Ennius critiques.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid Bombast and False Grandeur
rubrics_metrics.description: Those who aim at grandeur may fall into bombast; attempts at ease can lead to emasculation — balance is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for strength without inflated diction and ease without slippage into obscurity. Self-awareness and revision curb excesses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality Within Constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: Originality is desirable, but novel characters or inventions must be internally consistent; better to retell known tales with a singular stamp than to awkwardly alter facts and characters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not be a slavish translator; transfuse the soul of Greek sources rather than literal words. Avoid mere novelty for its own sake.

rubrics_metrics.name: Know Your Audience and Adapt
rubrics_metrics.description: Observe each age's temper (boy, youth, man, old) and impart to each the grace and finish suited to them; plays should meet the audience's expectations and capacities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write with awareness of audience demographics and tastes. Different stages of life respond to different emotional prompts and styles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-Criticism and Revision
rubrics_metrics.description: A true craftsman acts as his own censor: prune words unworthy of place, and restore dignity through careful revision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Repeatedly consider and revise; 'ponder your subject o'er not once nor twice'. Persistent mistakes (copyist who stumbles on same word) must be cured or abandoned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid Trying to Please Everyone
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not attempt to satisfy incompatible tastes simultaneously; a host cannot serve three guests each demanding different dishes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose a course and audience rather than pandering to every request. Attempting to please all will make all dissatisfied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order and Arrangement Can Elevate the Commonplace
rubrics_metrics.description: Skillful ordering and arrangement can make the cheap seem choice and the threadbare new.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Craft structure and sequence to enhance material; polished arrangement is a key mark of art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study Wisdom, Life, and Models
rubrics_metrics.description: The secret of writing well lies in wisdom: study Plato, life and manners, and Greek models; practice comprehension of duty, love, and public roles to inform sentiment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ground poetic inventiveness in knowledge of life and classical precedents; immersion in models refines taste and technique.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forgive Minor Slips but Not Recurrent Faults
rubrics_metrics.description: Minor blemishes in long works may be forgiven, but recurring or habitual mistakes (same word error, repeated discord) discredit the author.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tolerate occasional lapses; root out perpetual failures (copyist errors, musician who always strikes the same discord).

rubrics_metrics.name: Do Not Confuse Public Reward with Mastery
rubrics_metrics.description: Public applause often follows spectacle or bright costume rather than true poetic merit; beware measuring art by pocket-filling applause.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seek mastery that moves hearts (wring, rouse, soothe) rather than bread-and-butter success tied to crowd-pleasing showing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid Flattery as a Criterion of Quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Being rewarded by princes or patrons (as with Choerilus) does not validate poor verse; patronage may be inconsistent with artistic value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trust critical standards and craft rather than praise from interest or indifference; prefer works that withstand public and future tests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance Mirth and Morals; Teach and Please
rubrics_metrics.description: Mixing grave and gay can be effective if the work can both teach and give pleasure; the successful writer gains votes from varied audiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Integrate instruction and delight without sacrificing plausibility or taste; moralizing should not deaden enjoyment.
